raw.assessment: The incumbent delivered every ordered design and some small covers within 25–31 minutes, but its final fitting check discovers costly defects after cutting and sewing. Rework affected 5/8 large and 2/14 medium covers; this suggests a size-associated problem without establishing its cause. A common allowance is a candidate explanation, confounded by unmeasured cloth direction, design and operator. The concrete limiting observation is H2-O3: two customer failures involved rounded corners absent from reference tables, so passing those tables may not establish customer fit. The 37-minute median and ten observed installations do not establish next-batch success; estimated waste by weight also does not certify the area constraint.

openings.claim: The common cutting allowance may produce a systematic finished-dimension mismatch for larger sizes, causing some rework.
openings.delta: Move dimensional diagnosis before bulk cutting and distinguish allowance error from cutting or sewing variation.
openings.prediction: If the allowance is responsible, accurately cut and sewn larger covers will still show a consistent mismatch against verified target geometry; inconsistent transfer or seam errors would weaken that account.
openings.probe: Sew initial production covers before releasing the remaining cuts. Compare order, cutting-card, actual panel and finished dimensions, recording seam take-up, operator, design and cloth direction. Check fit and record cutting, sewing and adjustment time separately. Revise an allowance only after locating the mismatch.
assumptions: Initial units remain usable; measurement and any revision fit the existing machines, 350-unit budget and three-week deadline.
Any changed cut plan honors ordered sizes and designs, uses purchased stock within 8% area waste, and retains wash-test survival and tool-free removal.

openings.claim: Does corner geometry predict installation failure beyond disagreement between actual and nominal table dimensions?
openings.delta: Test the reference-table blind spot separately from nominal-size error.
openings.prediction: Failures at matched measured dimensions but different corner profiles support a geometry effect; failures tracking dimension discrepancies across profiles support a measurement explanation.
openings.probe: Request length, width and corner-profile measurements from the six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders where possible. Compare these with reference tables and record first placement on available measured customer tables. Treat unmatched comparisons as inconclusive.
assumptions: Customer participation permits useful comparisons within the delivery window.
Measurements clarify the specified table without substituting ordered size or design; any later construction change requires separate constraint verification.

raw.assessment: Size-linked rework, corner mismatch and variable length shrinkage support competing hypotheses, not established causes. Neither opening yet demonstrates 38 first-placement successes, wash durability or a 32-minute median. Preserve ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, area waste at or below 8%, two machines, the 350-unit ceiling and three-week deadline.

openings.claim: A concealed compliant corner pocket could accommodate rounded corners while retaining the ordered visible face: replace rigid inner pocket tension with a short washable elastic bridge sewn only to the cover.
openings.delta: Make the retention geometry locally compliant instead of requiring each table corner to match a rigid sewn pocket.
openings.prediction: With actual tabletop dimensions matched, compliance should improve first placement specifically at rounded corners without introducing visible slack on square corners; incorrect panel dimensions would still fail.
openings.probe: Obtain corner profiles and actual dimensions from willing customers. Compare rigid and reversibly basted compliant pockets on a retained or batch pilot cover against corresponding table geometry. Record placement, visible distortion and labor, then repeat after the stipulated five-cycle wash test. Cost materials before adoption and count prototype cloth in area-waste accounting.
assumptions: Customers can provide usable corner profiles.
A representative rounded-table trial can be arranged within the deadline.
Elastic survives washing and provides sufficient retention without visible distortion.

openings.claim: Does dimensional error arise before sewing, accumulate through seam construction, or emerge during washing, and does it scale with panel length?
openings.delta: Locate the stage and scaling of error before changing the common allowance; a proportional correction and a fixed seam correction imply different cutting cards.
openings.prediction: Proportional material change produces approximately stable percentage error; construction uptake produces error appearing after sewing, potentially concentrated at pockets. Both may coexist.
openings.probe: Delay bulk cutting. Mark and measure both axes before cutting, after cutting and after sewing on matched small/large pilots, holding design, direction and worker constant. Measure available offcuts in both axes through washing. Time each stage and verify revised nesting remains within 8% area waste before committing remaining stock.
assumptions: Matched ordered designs exist across sizes.
Measurements can distinguish the candidate error magnitudes.
Pilot timing fits the delivery window.

openings.claim: Large-cover mismatch may reflect common allowance, transfer/cutting error, seam uptake or proportional wash change; causes may coexist.
openings.discriminator: Consistent mismatch despite accurate construction supports allowance error; stage onset and fixed versus percentage error distinguish alternatives.
openings.probe: Delay bulk cutting; compare order/card, both panel axes and finished dimensions on matched small/large pilots. Control design, direction and worker; record seam uptake and stage times. Wash offcuts measuring both axes; verify revised nesting by area.
openings.uncertainty: Size association is confounded; width shrinkage is unknown. Matching, measurement resolution and usable pilots remain uncertain.

openings.claim: Rounded corners may explain customer failures independently of actual-versus-nominal dimensions.
openings.discriminator: At matched actual dimensions, profile-linked failures support geometry; failures tracking dimension discrepancies support measurement error.
openings.probe: Request dimensions and corner profiles from six willing customers, prioritizing nominal-only orders; compare references and first placement on available measured tables.
openings.uncertainty: Unmatched comparisons are inconclusive; participation and representative tables may be unavailable.

openings.claim: A concealed washable elastic bridge may make corner pockets accommodate rounded profiles.
openings.discriminator: Improved rounded-corner placement without square-corner slack at matched dimensions; panel errors should persist.
openings.probe: Compare rigid and reversibly basted compliant pockets before/after five wash cycles; record distortion, placement and labor. Cost materials and account for prototype cloth.
openings.uncertainty: Elastic durability, retention, representative trials and deadline feasibility unproven.

lineage.reason: Combined allowance diagnosis with stage/scaling distinctions.
Preserved cutting, sewing, washing and both-axis discrimination.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize D1/D2; condition D3 on trials. Honor ordered sizes/designs, purchased stock, <=8% area waste, five-cycle survival, tool-free removal, two machines, <=350 cost and three weeks. Weight-estimated waste does not certify area. No opening establishes >=38/40 first placements, all correct designs or <=32-minute median.
